user.title: UltraWideLock
user.description: Add live UWB data, history, events, and dashboard cards. Reading works without changes to Matter Server. Enable writable controls only if you want to change UltraWideLock-specific distances and action policies from Home Assistant.

data_description.enable_writable_controls: Requires installing the bundled custom-cluster schema in the Matter Server app. The next step provides instructions.

writable_setup.title: Enable writable controls
writable_setup.description:
Complete these steps before finishing setup:

1. Open the **Terminal & SSH** app.
2. Run `sh /homeassistant/custom_components/uwb_matter/install_matter_schema.sh`.
3. Open **Settings > Apps > Matter Server > Configuration**.
4. Press the three dots and choose **Edit in YAML**.
5. Add:
```yaml
matter_server_env_vars:
  - NODE_OPTIONS=--import=/config/ultrawidelock-cluster.mjs
```
6. Save the app configuration. Confirm below, finish this integration flow, then restart Matter Server and Home Assistant.

data.setup_confirmed: I installed the schema and added the Matter Server environment variable

error.setup_not_confirmed: Complete the Matter Server steps and confirm before continuing.

init.title: UltraWideLock settings
init.description: Choose whether to manage live-data freshness, detected UWB devices, or a standard Matter lock binding.

matter_binding.title: Matter lock binding
matter_binding.description: Choose the UltraWideLock whose standard Matter Door Lock binding you want to add or remove. This integration changes only the UltraWideLock Binding Table. The target lock ACL remains under your manual control.

binding_action.title: Matter lock binding
binding_action.description: Choose whether to add or remove a bound Matter lock.

add_binding.title: Add a bound lock
add_binding.description: Choose the Matter Door Lock endpoint to add to the UltraWideLock Binding Table. After the binding has been written and verified, the next screen explains how to grant the required ACL permission manually in Matter Server.

manual_acl_add.title: Grant the binding access in Matter Server
manual_acl_add.description:
The binding has been added to **{source_lock}**. The target lock must now grant this UltraWideLock permission before bound lock and unlock commands can work. The integration will not change the ACL automatically.

**Target lock:** `{target_lock}` (node `{target_node}`)
**UltraWideLock:** `{source_lock}` (node `{source_node}`)

1. Go to **Settings > Apps > Matter Server**.
2. Press **Open Web UI**.
3. Select **{target_lock}**.
4. Open **Endpoint 0**.
5. Press the **settings wheel** in the top-right corner.
6. Switch **Developer Mode** on and close the settings.
7. Open **AccessControl**.
8. Expand **Access Control — ACL Entries**.
9. First check whether an **Operate (3)** or higher entry for **{source_lock}** already targets **EP {target_endpoint} · DoorLock (0x0101)** and shows **backs binding**. If it does, do not create a duplicate and continue with the confirmation below.
10. Otherwise, press **Add ACL entry**.
11. Set **Privilege** to **Operate (3)**.
12. Under **Known nodes**, choose **{source_lock}** (node `{source_node}`).
13. Set **Endpoint** to **EP {target_endpoint}** and **Cluster** to **DoorLock (0x0101)**.
14. Press **Add target**, then press **Add**.
15. Verify that the **Relationship** column shows **backs binding** and your UltraWideLock.

If **Add ACL entry** is disabled because the list is full, do not delete the controller's protected Administer entry. Review obsolete entries first. You can later delete this permission from the same ACL overview.

data.manual_acl_confirmed: I added the ACL entry and verified the binding relationship

data_description.manual_acl_confirmed: Only confirm after Matter Server shows the UltraWideLock ACL entry with Operate access to the selected DoorLock endpoint.

remove_binding.title: Remove a bound lock
remove_binding.description: Choose the Door Lock binding to remove. The target lock ACL is not changed automatically; cleanup instructions follow after the binding has been removed.

confirm_remove_binding.title: Confirm binding removal
confirm_remove_binding.description: Remove the binding from **{source_lock}** to **{target_lock}**? This stops the UltraWideLock from targeting that lock. It does not yet remove the permission stored in the target lock ACL.

data.confirm_binding_removal: I want to remove this binding

manual_acl_remove.title: Remove the unused ACL permission
manual_acl_remove.description:
The binding has been removed from **{source_lock}**. Its ACL permission may still remain on **{target_lock}** and can now be removed manually.

**Target lock:** `{target_lock}` (node `{target_node}`)
**UltraWideLock:** `{source_lock}` (node `{source_node}`)

1. Go to **Settings > Apps > Matter Server**.
2. Press **Open Web UI**.
3. Select **{target_lock}**.
4. Open **Endpoint 0**.
5. Press the **settings wheel** in the top-right corner.
6. Switch **Developer Mode** on and close the settings.
7. Open **AccessControl**.
8. Expand **Access Control — ACL Entries**.
9. Find the **Operate (3)** entry whose subject is **{source_lock}** (node `{source_node}`) and whose target is **EP {target_endpoint} · DoorLock (0x0101)**.
10. Press **Delete** on that entry and confirm.

Because the binding has already been removed, the Relationship column may no longer say **backs binding**. Identify the entry using the UltraWideLock node and DoorLock target shown above. Never delete the protected Administer entry for the current controller. Leaving the UWL entry in place does not recreate the binding, but it leaves unused permission on the target lock.

data.manual_acl_confirmed: I reviewed the ACL and removed the UWL permission, or intentionally chose to retain it

data_description.manual_acl_confirmed: Removing the ACL entry follows least privilege. Retaining it leaves permission available if you recreate the binding later.

data_freshness.title: UWB data freshness
data_freshness.description: This setting is independent of device names. It determines how long Home Assistant may show the latest live distance and movement when Matter updates stop arriving. After this timeout the data is marked stale and live values are cleared.

data_description.stale_timeout_seconds: Use a short value to hide frozen data quickly. The default is 15 seconds.

credentials.title: Detected UWB devices
credentials.description: Choose a detected credential to give it a friendly name or remove its automatically created occupancy sensor.

credential.title: UWB device settings
credential.description: Configure UWB credential `{credential_id}`. Its occupancy sensor turns on only when this specific device is in range of the selected UltraWideLock. Turn the option off to remove that sensor.

data.create_presence_sensor: Create an occupancy sensor for this device

data_description.friendly_name: For example: Personal iPhone or Apple Watch.
data_description.create_presence_sensor: Creates a standard Home Assistant occupancy binary sensor attached to every UltraWideLock that sees this credential. Disable it to remove the sensor while retaining the friendly name.
